column1: # Field batch: screen.OptionsScreen (21 fields, was 100% obfuscated).
# The class builds a settings dialog: a panel image, a ScrollPane wrapping a Container of ListBox
# rows, one ListBox per option. Every ListBox is created through createListBox(id, ...) and the
# SAME id is the case label in handleWidgetAction, whose body calls the matching UserConfig setter
# and whose i18n label confirms the option - so each field is pinned by THREE independent sources:
# the createListBox(id) call, the switch case in handleWidgetAction, and the label string.
# Evidence (id -> field -> case -> UserConfig setter / label):
#  100 p  scrollKeyLeft     case 100 -> setTouchDeviceFlag(6)          (label "Scroll Key Left")
#  101 q  scrollKeyRight    case 101 -> setTouchDeviceFlag(7)          (label "Scroll Key Right")
#  102 r  scrollKeyUp       case 102 -> setTouchDeviceFlag(8)          (label "Scroll Key Up")
#  103 s  scrollKeyDown     case 103 -> setTouchDeviceFlag(9)          (label "Scroll Key Down")
#  a  background       = new NinePatchImage(GuiAssets.i())            (i() is the panel nine-patch)
#  b  scrollPane       = new ScrollPane(GuiAssets.k())               (k() is the ScrollBarStyle)
#  c  contentContainer  = the Container that holds every option row
#  e  languages        = the Language[] passed in (incl. the default null entry)
#  t  contentHeight    = running y offset accumulated while adding rows, compared to scrollPane height
#  u  selectedLanguage  = this.u = UserConfig.getLanguage(); compared in case 0/1
# Descriptors come from javap: do not edit them, the renamer matches on them.
# Columns: owner <TAB> kind <TAB> old <TAB> descriptor <TAB> new
